title: A cube-root phase transition in tree-child networks and the enumeration threshold for galled networks
summary: We prove two surprising results about phylogenetic networks. First, we show that the structure of tree-child networks with $n$ leaves and $k$ reticulation nodes undergoes a sharp phase transition at $n^{1/3}$: if $k=o(n^{1/3})$, then a random tree-child network is almost surely a semi-simplex tree-child network, whereas if $k/n^{1/3}\rightarrow\infty$ and $k=o(n^{1/2})$, it is almost surely not.
